html:
Zeila is an ancient port on the Gulf of Aden in northwest Somalia, where Islam arrived very early, by tradition in the first century of the Muslim era.

Close to Arabia across the water, it traded with Yemen and the Ethiopian highlands. An old mosque there is said to have faced both Jerusalem and Mecca, though its date is uncertain. By the Middle Ages Zeila was a Muslim city and the port of the Ifat and Adal sultanates, which fought the Christian kings of Ethiopia.

Islam spread from such ports to the Somali clans inland, and today Somalis are almost all Muslim. The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited Zeila in 1331. Later the port declined in favour of Berbera and Djibouti.
sum: Zeila is an ancient port on the Gulf of Aden in northwest Somalia, where Islam arrived very early, by tradition in the first century of the Muslim era.
